reproduction_review.limitations: Single cached RG task, deterministic HTTP response, real servers/renderers/materializer/value credit. No model, GPU, whole TrainSink publication or multiturn proof.

source_findings: OrchestratorConfig.resolve_env_config sets max_seq_len only on legacy training environments.
Verifier utils/response_utils.py parse_response_tokens clips returned token arrays after full response parsing. Full message text remains the reward and peer-context source.
Verifier v1/legacy.py _to_v1_response preserves original call Usage and finish_reason. _v1_stop_condition separately maps truncation stop names.

Verifier v1/trace.py Branch.num_total_tokens uses last_usage.total_tokens and num_output_tokens uses aggregate usage.completion_tokens. Both remain physical provider counters after legacy clipping. Do not replace these with retained training counts in length penalty or batching.
TrainSink captures ValueTrajectory after materialization. This is the ownership boundary: truncation after capture or only in policy packing is too late to preserve critic credit geometry.

Filters inspect branches directly; algorithm base reference scoring, Echo and Tether fallback also consume iter_trainable_branches. Materialized-samples-only clipping would leave inconsistent training consumers.

from_episode currently shares node/call objects through model_construct. Projection must allocate owned node arrays; mutating the returned Rollout would otherwise mutate the canonical physical Episode.

recommended_contract.configuration: Explicit opt-in per-training-environment projection profile, default absent. Positive max_seq_len resolved to actor sequence length for an explicitly migrated config; no automatic native default change.
recommended_contract.boundary: One pure helper projects an upstream vf.Trace before from_episode constructs Rollout. Input Episode remains byte-identical. Returned canonical Trace is explicitly a training projection, not claimed to be the physical source.
recommended_contract.initial_admission: One successful model call, one linear text-only branch, complete well-aligned token/mask/logprob arrays. Reject requested projection for unsupported multiturn, branching, tools, multimodal, routed-expert or kept-token sidecars. No restriction is added when projection is absent.
recommended_contract.geometry: Clone nodes and slice token_ids/mask/is_content by remaining prefix cap; slice sampling logprobs by retained sampled-token count. Retain empty suffix nodes, full messages, calls, raw Usage, finish reasons, rewards and task data. This preserves graph/call identity while changing only training-visible arrays.
recommended_contract.provenance: Retain original physical trace or Episode in an excluded ownership field if its lifetime otherwise ends. Persist a clear projection receipt: profile, limit, original stop/truncation, physical and retained token/action counts. Serialized projected records must be labeled. Do not invent raw usage or overwrite physical call finish reasons.
recommended_contract.truncation: Projected trace exposes effective truncation when clipping occurred, using an existing canonical truncation stop marker and recording the original reason. Exact legacy stop-condition spelling is not universal: RG maps max_turns_reached to max_turns. Keep physical flags accessible separately.
recommended_contract.no_actions: Prompt at or beyond the cap produces no sampled training tokens; existing no-sample and group/LOO rejection handles the rollout. No fake terminal action or critic update.
recommended_contract.credit: Existing critic snapshot/GAE receives projected samples. Full-response reward remains assigned to the last retained action. Existing critic sequence cap and privileged-prefix rules remain unchanged.
recommended_contract.other_consumers: All filters/reference scoring/Echo/Tether/materialization see the same projected canonical trace through existing Rollout paths. LOO full message text and actual call finish reasons remain unchanged. Existing raw provider usage counters keep historical length-penalty and batching meaning.

acceptance_gates: No-profile native path remains byte-for-byte and numerically unchanged; original Episode bytes remain unchanged under projection too.

Actual old/native producer cases below, equal to, and above both prompt and completion boundaries; compare masks/logprobs/actions, full reward, raw Usage, effective truncation and owned value targets.
Actual TrainSink publication and group-LOO context equality for mixed rewards with a clipped sibling; prompt-overflow sibling yields the same whole-group eligibility behavior.
Tail-only gibberish/repetition must be ignored in projected filters exactly as legacy; retained-prefix defect remains detected. This checks cohort selection, not only array lengths.
Unsupported topology and sidecars fail explicitly before sample/value publication; no-profile versions continue working.
Keep source and projected records separately inspectable; destructive downstream sample cleanup cannot mutate the physical Episode or owned critic trajectory.

later_dependency_pair.finding: Reviewed TrainClient, AgentConfig and TurnTokens definitions: no equivalent post-response actor-training-limit option. Agent/input/output limits and renderer max_prompt_len change generation/admission, so cannot reproduce full-text scoring plus clipped training. Later verifier has logical/effective multimodal token separation and version spans; projection must explicitly reject or support those arrays during that future upgrade. This bounded current-stack projection does not require upgrading the producer dependencies.
